text: Lilmoth Dock is a short pull east of here, passenger. It is a mess of small craft when you get there. Alten Merihall is a long haul down the coast, east-south-east. I charge for every channel on the way.

There is a longboat drawn up on the bank, a short walk south. Lifts-The-Sacks is the only hand here who loads a boat properly. I would sooner watch him than the soldiers, Sees-No-Shade and Rakhee-Tul, who guard the south side of the plantation.

Lilmoth sits over shallow water, so the big ships cannot dock. They anchor out. Boats like mine carry the goods in. Since Lilmoth fell, Alten Merihall has taken much of the bay's outside trade. That is more water for the rest of us to cross.

There is a large ship on the shore, a short walk south. A captain's journal and some armour lie beside it, a little nearer. Her crew lost her and still say she ran herself aground. Go and look, passenger. Judge the water for yourself.

I am Reads-The-Shallows. I run a flat boat with the plantation's rice to Lilmoth. I know every channel between here and the walls. I am waiting for a full load and a fair wind. I would rather leave before the steward changes his mind about the price.
You wish to go to Lolmoth, visitor? Then listen. It is the walled part of Lilmoth, about two hundred paces east-north-east of here. East-north-east, mind, not east.

This is the yard of the house, visitor. I keep it, and the stores. Do you have business at the house? The food barrels and the ingredient barrel stand about fifteen paces west of here, and the meat barrels about fifteen paces west-south-west. Please do not touch them.
Hereguard Plantation grows rice. Lilmoth buys it. I see what leaves this yard, visitor. All of it.

I am Hurz-Weel. I keep the yard and the stores. The steward wants a hand within call, so here I stay. I was born on this plantation. I have never been further than Lilmoth. There is a great deal here to look after, visitor.

The house servants? Folds-The-Linen is about five paces south-south-east of here, and Mazei-Tul about five paces north. You will find them sitting, I think. They sit and I carry the barrels. Go to them if you must, visitor.
Look down, friend. An iron spear lies on the ground, five paces south-south-west of me, and anyone may pick it up. Take it before the goats find it interesting. Ha.
This is the yard, friend. Every job comes past me here. The goats and the chickens keep the far side, about ten paces west-north-west. Is that not so, my fine ones?
Here a debt is paid in work. An arbitrator turns the loss into months. We count them in nushmeekos, the thankless ones. Work them all and it is over.
An owing can be sold on, friend. Whoever is owed the months may sell them to a person who needs hands. The worker goes with them, sacks and all.
I am Lifts-The-Sacks. I load the rice and do the heavy work others will not do. My uncle ran up a debt. I am working off the months. Do not pity me, friend. I am strong. The flood is coming. Ha.
Reads-The-Shallows, the boat captain, waits about ten paces north-north-west of here. Go and speak to the captain, friend. I like that one. They thank me.
Gleamblossom, hatchling, if you have the patience to look for it. One grows about sixty paces south of here.
The hands come to the cooking spit when the work is done. That is why I stand here. It is about five paces west-south-west of me. Go and sit by it, hatchling. Eat something.
I am Salith. I came up from Lilmoth to sell to the hands. I stayed because I am the only one here who feeds them properly. Hungry people buy, hatchling, so here I stand.
I sell food and small goods, hatchling, to anyone with the coin and to a few who owe me for last week. Do not tell me you have eaten when your ribs say otherwise. Eat something.

Okan-Wul is usually about five paces north of here; I mother that hatchling, whatever they say. Stares-At-Clouds is about twenty-five paces north-north-east, lazy and sweet. For Uleesh, go about forty-five paces east to the shallows below the walls of Lilmoth; he fishes there. He is the most honest man outside the walls.

Start with the huts, stranger. The hands live in them, about thirty-five paces west of here. More stand a little further off to the west-north-west. Look at the joints and the roofs. You will see why I am never idle.
Do you see the stone wall along the east side, stranger? It is about fifteen paces south-west of here.

What if a town could be built so it did not have to be built twice, stranger? Lilmoth was destroyed long ago and built again, smaller and lower, on stilts. The drowned old quarter has not been rebuilt.

Lilmoth was destroyed long ago. It was built again as a stilt town, smaller and lower than before. The old quarter is under the water and has not been rebuilt. Tell me, stranger, what do the houses look like where you come from?

I am Okan-Wul. I build and mend the huts here. I stay near Salith's stall between jobs. She is the one who really runs this plantation, whatever the title says. One day I mean to build something that will not rot in a season.
I am Okan-Wul, stranger. I keep the hands' huts standing. It is hard work with this timber. If I had good timber and someone to show me how stone is laid, you would see something.

The carpenter's workbench is about thirty paces south-west of here. The armour workbench is about thirty paces south-south-west, a little further round. Look at how the benches are jointed while you are there, stranger.

I build and mend the huts on the east side. I do it with what I am given. The carpenter's workbench is about thirty paces south-west of here, and the armour workbench is about thirty paces south-south-west. The hands would be better housed with timber as good as the house gets, stranger.

Slaughterfish, dry-foot. Twenty paces north of here the water is full of them. More lie ten paces off to the south-west. They take my catch off the line. I do not forgive it. Wade slow and do not splash.
Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore about thirty paces south-south-west. They are slow, but I leave them alone, and so should you.
Lolmoth is the walled part of Lilmoth. Walk east-north-east from here, about a hundred paces. You will meet the walls. I think those walls keep out the wrong people.
Hereguard Plantation is west-south-west, a little over a hundred paces. Ask for Salith when you get there. She sells me my bait. The plantation pays its hands too little, but Salith is fair.
Wild leeks grow on the bank, east-south-east of here, about a hundred paces. Keep to the bank when you go. The lily pads are mine. I do not want anyone splashing about on them.

Hm. I do not tell this to everyone. There is a giant crab called Old Salty in the shallows to the south-south-west, about ninety paces from here. He is old. He is not to be bothered. Leave him be, dry-foot.
I am Uleesh. I fish the shallows below the walls and sell my catch inside. Rent in there costs more than fish pay, so I live out here. I have fished this water twenty years and I know it.
Lolmoth. The walled part of Lilmoth. East of here… a little over a hundred paces. You will see the wall. Tell me, did the sky look like this where you came from?
Giant lichen. West of here, and a little south. A hundred paces, perhaps more. I was watching the water… forgive me. Yes, there. Past the huts.
The hands sleep in the huts. Forty paces west of here. I stand out beyond them, because the water comes in this way. The flood always does. Mind the water.
A holder owed months can sell them. To someone who needs hands. And the worker goes with them. The worker is not asked or told. I would have liked to be told.
An Argonian kept long from his own Hist… fades. The colour thins. The markings go soft. It comes back, when the person goes home. Look at me. Do I look thin to you?
Stares-At-Clouds. I watch the water here. I call out when it rises. And the clouds. And the birds, when there are birds. You came from upriver, I think. What did the sky look like there?
Nightshade grows a short walk east-north-east of here, guest. Gather it there if you must, but do not bring it into the kitchen.
We keep the tables, the bed and the dresser a short walk west of here, in the plantation house. Wipe your feet before you step inside, guest.
The dresser stands west-south-west of here, a little further than the house tables. Leave what is inside it alone, guest. I will not say more of it unless I know you better.
I am Folds-The-Linen. I keep this house clean and its linen folded. I stay close in case I am called, because we do not like to be found wanting.

Looks-At-Books keeps her shelf a short walk west of here. She is the only person in this place worth your breath, guest. Hurz-Weel keeps the yard to the north-north-west, close by; he tramps mud through the house, so keep him from the door.
Mm. The dock, rider? East. It is about four hundred paces, and the way is crowded. Too many feet, too much noise. No horse would thank you for it.

Horses, rider. Ten paces west-north-west of here, and the saddled black is the finest of them. Look at the stirrup leathers and the way the coat shines. I look after them better than anyone else here.
Cows, if you want cows. Twenty paces west, and more thirty paces south. They are dull company beside the horses. Mm.
Me? I am a house servant. Mm. The house has plenty of hands, so I mind the horses on the north side, where they stand. I would rather be a rider than a servant, if you must know.
Lifts-The-Sacks? Mm. Forty-five paces east, in the middle of the yard. Lifts-The-Sacks helps me with the feed, so that one is a good sort, rider.
The dock lies north-east of here, walker, a short walk. The walled part of Lilmoth, which the maps call Lolmoth, lies north-north-west and a little farther. We do not go to either unless we must.

This is a village of a few families, walker. We live on the open marsh. You are standing at the cooking spit. The carpenter's bench is five paces south-south-east of it, and a food barrel five paces east-south-east.
There is a second hearth thirty paces west, on the edge of the village, with food barrels, a cooking pot and a bed. The children have to wade to those barrels. We need a dry season.
Lilmoth has no single ruler, walker. A council of powerful merchants governs it and pays guards to patrol the streets. They send collectors to us for fish that never passed their gate.
In Lilmoth people take their quarrels to their elders, retired Shadowscales among them, not to a court. Here a quarrel ends at the spit. I hear it out.
I am Flaa Heet, headman of this village. I lead a few families who live on the open marsh and pay no rent to Lilmoth. I want no seat on the merchant council, walker. I say so before anyone offers.
Tseeta sells from her stall ten paces north of here, walker. She haggles too hard. We are better for her all the same. Okeeh-Jas sells from hers five paces south-south-west.
Wild leeks, big one? Huge, huge ones, about forty-five paces north-west of here, by the fish barrels. Is that a sharp knife on your belt?
Emperor Parasol Moss hangs about sixty paces north of here. It is a huge walk, big one. Have you got a good knife for it? Let me see.
That is our rowboat, big one, drawn up about twenty paces east-north-east of here. Have you ever rowed one? Would you take me out in it, to the north-east, just once? Do not tell my mother.
I am a hatchling. I am small, but I am going to be a boat captain, big one. I practise on the frogs. They do not listen yet. Why are your boots so muddy?
Flaa Heet is the headman. He knows everything, big one. Everything! He stands by the cooking spit, about twenty paces south of here. Will you tell him I sent you?
Hums-To-The-Rain is usually about twenty paces south-south-west of here, on the west side of the village. Singing, singing, singing. Do you sing, big one? Please do not.

One, two: the Docks lie east-north-east of here, about four hundred paces, past Lilmoth Dock. That is where the real money is, buyer. Hereguard Plantation is west-north-west, about two hundred and sixty paces. Good trade.
I am Tseeta. This is the first stall you meet from the dock, because I chose the north side for it. I sell the village's surplus: fish, roots and small goods. Buy something and I will tell you more.
Food and small goods, buyer. Fish, roots, whatever the village has over. Show me your purse and I will show you the best of it.
Okeeh-Jas keeps the other stall, twenty paces south of here. Watch him smile while he undersells me, buyer. Then count your change. Good trade.
I sell before the light goes, buyer. Everyone here keeps the fish in barrels fifty paces north-north-west of here. I am the one who carries it to you.
Mm, you want plants, traveller. Gourds grow a short walk north-north-east of here, and a swamp fungal pod a little beyond them.
Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow together further on, still north-north-east.
This is a quiet village, traveller. I mend its nets on the west side, between the two hearths, where they dry. Mm, do not step on the rope.
We keep a meat barrel for the village out on the marsh, a short walk north-north-west of here. I would sooner keep to the marsh north of us than go near Lilmoth's walls.
Mm. An Argonian kept long from their own Hist fades. The colour thins and the markings go soft. They come back when the person goes home. I would rather not say more of it, traveller.
About ten miles from Lilmoth there is a wall of mangroves, so thick that hardly anyone can pass. The old story says the roots were giant spiders once. I like hearing it, but I would not walk there.
I am Hums-To-The-Rain. I mend the nets here and gather what grows on the marsh. Mm, I came from a tribe inland, years ago.
I have not said which tribe, traveller. I will not say today. Ask me about the nets instead.

Oh, the boat, dear? There is a rowboat drawn up at the south landing, fifteen paces from my stall, just down the way, you see? If it is Lilmoth Dock you want, that is a good walk north-east of here, a couple of hundred paces and a bit, so mind your feet on the planks.

Oh, you want the old tale? Lilmoth was destroyed long ago and then built again, smaller and lower, a stilt town. The drowned old quarter has not been rebuilt. I have never heard anyone say why, though I have heard everyone say something.

Rumours, dear, now you are speaking my tongue! There is a drinker called Deep-In-His-Cups sitting out on the shore track, about a hundred and fifty paces north-east of here. He talks to anyone who stays, you see? I think he knows more than he lets on, so stay a while and keep your ears open.

Me? I sell from this stall where the rowboat comes in, so I trade with anyone who lands. I married into this village, but I still talk like the city. I am not sorry for it. Now tell me, where have you come from, and is that a fresh cut on your arm?

Food and small goods, dear, all of it from this stall. You can look all you like. Whatever you may have heard about what I sell, hear it from me instead. I laugh at my own prices, so you may as well laugh with me and then pay them.
Listen, friend. When the rain comes, a fighter wants a roof. There is a door that leads indoors about sixty paces east of here.
Mind yourself, friend. The dead walk outside Lilmoth's walls. There are walking dead about a hundred paces north-north-west of here. I would not go to them with empty hands.
Lilmoth Dock lies about eighty paces north-east of here. Go and see it, but the council's guards at the gate called us unlicensed blades and turned us away.
I am Breaks-The-Oar, friend. My fists belong to whoever pays the band. I am the one who talks terms. Have you work this week?

The band is camped here, friend. Keeps-Both-Edges is about five paces west of me. I trust him with my life and my purse. Heem-Tsal the fire mage is about ten paces west-south-west. He is cleverer than the rest of us, and too proud for his own good.
You wish to find a Dwemer ruin, ojel? One is marked on the map. It lies far to the east, about four hundred and thirty-five paces from where I stand.
Jazbay, lavender and juniper grow together about fifty-five paces north-west of here, and any alchemist would call that an uncommonly convenient bed.

West of Lilmoth lies the Ixtaxh Xanmeer, silted and flooded again, so that only its topmost chamber stands above the mud. I have wanted to see the rest of it for a long time. I would need someone to carry the lamp.

In the lowlands east of Lilmoth stands the Xinchei-Konu Monument. It is an old stone calendar that is said to change the weather. It has a keeper of its own. Lilmoth's Hist is tended in the open behind a wall. The tree-minder's post rotates so that a single person never listens to it alone. I asked to sit beside it and take notes. I found the answer narrow-minded.

I cast fire for this band, ojel; when I am not casting I read whatever I can get my hands on. I stand apart from the others because I find their talk tiresome; I joined them for passage south. I have not yet found a reason to leave.
A bookseller named Looks-At-Books keeps her shelf at Hereguard Plantation, about three hundred and sixty paces west of here. I have heard of it more than once. I intend to see that shelf for myself.
You there. Why ask what I would rather you never met? More dead walk among the gravestones north of Lolmoth, some two hundred and fifty paces north-west of here. Keep away from them.
A crocodile lies in the water west of here, about two hundred and forty paces off. Do you wade in rivers whose bottom you cannot see?
These dead trees on the shore track, twenty paces north-east of here, are where the band camps. We do not intend to stay.
Why do you want to know? I fight with a blade in each hand and I keep the band's watch. I was a guard once. I will not say for whom.

Do you mean the two by the leeks to the north? Sheeh-Vos is sixty paces north-north-east of here, and Waits-For-Lanterns about the same to the north-east. I do not trust either of them. Keep your hand on your purse.

Ah, my good friend, the village, Flaa Heet's village, is out on the marsh about a hundred and forty-five paces south-west of here. The dock is only fifty-odd paces north-north-east, where the boats are. Mind you, I know the dock better. I knew every plank of it once. Now where was I going with that?

Ah, my good friend, you ask me about boats. You could not have asked a better man. Lilmoth sits over water too shallow for the big ships, so they lie out at anchor and the lighters bring the goods in. I was a lighterman, did I tell you that? And out in the deep water are the sea-drakes, great crocodile things with paddles for legs. I never once liked the look of them.

Rumours, is it, my good friend? Well, I sit here and I see things. There are three dead Dunmer lying at the east end of the dock, about seventy paces north-north-east of here. They lie unburied, which is not right, not right at all. Have you got a drop of anything about you, for an old man who talks?

My name is Deep-In-His-Cups, my good friend. I have earned it. I will not say I have not. I was a lighterman once, with a lighter of my own to handle. I will tell you the whole of that story if you will sit and listen, as others will not. The guards at the dock move me on, so I sit out here. I see more than they think.
Keep your voice down, cousin. Wild leeks grow right here, about twenty paces west-south-west. Pull them slowly, as a gatherer would, eh?
Past the bodies at the dock's east end there is a chest, about sixty paces east-north-east of here. Look at it before anyone else does, cousin, eh? I would go myself, but I am watching the dock.
Dunmer corpses lie unlooted about fifty-five paces north-east of here. Be quick, before the guards come. Do not tell Waits-For-Lanterns that I sent you.

I am Sheeh-Vos, cousin. I gather what is dropped at the dock and, well, I take what is not. I crouch among the leeks so that I look like a gatherer, eh? Waits-For-Lanterns works with me. I do not like him.
Deep-In-His-Cups sits about twenty-five paces south-south-east of here. He sees everything at the dock, cousin. He remembers only half of what he sees. Do not let him see your purse.

Ah, my friend… a careful question. I do like a careful question. The walking dead wander outside the walls, some hundred and fifteen paces north-west of here. They are not patient creatures. I have never had much use for anything that hurries.
Hunger, my friend, is only a matter of planning. Gourds grow some eighty-five paces west-south-west of here, and a man may eat his fill on this shore if he is willing to walk a little.
You ask what is worth the finding. I might answer that, my friend. There is a door below the walls, about a hundred and five paces west-north-west of here. It leads indoors. It is out of the way.

My friend, I do not give this away. I would not have you think it is free. Near the graves north of Lolmoth, perhaps a hundred and forty-five paces north-west of here, there is a trapdoor in the ground. It leads down under the city. Do not trouble yourself with the chest beside it; someone with less patience emptied it already.
I am Waits-For-Lanterns, my friend. I plan small jobs and I wait for the dark to do them. I am a professional. This is merely a slow season.

Halt, citizen. Keep off the shore. Old Salty, a giant crab, holds the shallows forty-five paces east-south-east. Giant mudcrabs sit on the shore sixty paces east-north-east. I hold my post well back from the water. I was told to.
State your business, citizen. The Docks lie east, six hundred paces, a long walk. Sheathe that weapon first, and do not wander.

I am Sees-No-Shade, hired to guard the south side of the plantation. I face the water because whatever comes, comes from the shore. Nothing happens on my watch, citizen. State your business or move along.
Rakhee-Tul holds the easier post, five paces north of here, and sleeps on it, citizen. Go and see for yourself.

Advice, boss? Free, and worth what you pay. If your gear is hanging loose, there is an armour workbench some twenty-five paces north-north-east of here. Go on, I will not report you for using it, which is more than Sees-No-Shade, the other guard, would do.
You want to know what bites, boss? Fly amanita grows about forty paces west-south-west of here, red cap, white spots, very pretty. Do not eat it. I only say so because someone always does.

Between us, boss, the wreck has barely been touched. There is iron and leather armour, weapons, a silver plate and a captain's journal by the beached ship, about ninety paces south of here. A passage door near the ship, about a hundred paces south, leads in. I would go before somebody else has the same idea.
Rakhee-Tul. I guard the south side with Sees-No-Shade. I do it from a bit nearer the yard, where the shade is. I took the post for the pay, boss. I will not pretend otherwise.
I read of it before I sell it, reader, so this I can say from the page. Once, a foreigner without a licence was kept to Lilmoth's docks and barred from the city.
A debt here is paid in work, reader. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour, and the months are counted in nushmeekos. When the months are worked, it is over.
I am Looks-At-Books, reader. I sell what I have read. I keep it out of the rain. Mind the pages.

I have the four volumes of The Argonian Account. I would rather sell them together than singly. I have The Lusty Argonian Maid, volumes 1 and 2, and The Sultry Argonian Bard, volume 1. There are Short History of Morrowind and Welcome to Black Marsh besides, with rolls of paper, inkwells and quills. Mind the pages.
Folds-The-Linen keeps the house, about fifteen paces east of here. I find her good company, reader.

My table is on the west side of the plantation house, among its tables, where the books keep dry. The house has a bed about five paces east-south-east of here. Damp ruins the books, so I keep them dry, reader.

Easy water, traveller. Keep away from the south-south-east, because a bear and her cubs roam a short walk that way. That bear took my goat last season. I have not forgiven her. A little farther on a tree mother lives in the woods. You should stay well clear of her.

You want the way, traveller? I can give you three. A Dwemer ruin lies a short walk east-south-east of here. Alten Merihall lies a good walk south-east down the coast. Lilmoth Dock lies about as far west, though it is all guards and no business. If it is Alten Merihall you want, my boat will take you there and spare your feet.

This is the Docks, where boats tie up. I keep mine at the head of the landing. A large ship lies west-south-west of here, a short walk off, with a door aboard. If you need a good hand with a boat, ask for Wades-Late, who is the best on the Docks.

Since Lilmoth fell, Alten Merihall has taken much of the bay's outside trade. That is where the money is now. Out in the deep water off Lilmoth live the sea-drakes, which are crocodile-like beasts with paddle legs. I have no wish to meet one.

I am Seeks-The-Channel. I run a boat out of the Docks. I wait here at the head of the landing between fares. I chose the Docks over Lilmoth Dock because here I am asked for nothing but the fare. I mean to take you somewhere worth the going, if you can pay.
Gourds, outsider. About twenty paces north-north-west of here. I remember what a gourd cost last season. I charge that for mine. Do not tell me the ones you pick are cheaper.
Houses open onto the Docks here. One door is about fifteen paces south of my stall, another about twenty paces south-east. Keep the cows away from my goods when you pass, outsider.
I am Ushaa-Mei. I sell food to the families of the Docks, and to anyone who lands. I keep to this side, between the houses. I remember what everything cost last season. I charge that.
I sell food and small goods. Look all you like, outsider, but hands off what you have not paid for. The weight is true and the price is last season's. Bring good coin.
Plaits-The-Reed sits about five paces west of here. Go and talk to her. I like her.

Sir, miss, may I ask a serious thing? Deathbell, nightshade and jazbay grow together about fifty paces south-east of here. Does it hurt very much, to be poisoned by them? I would like to know before I go near.

Miss, this is the Docks. I sit in the middle by the fire so I hear everything the grown-ups say. Two cows graze not far east-north-east of here, about fifteen paces. Chases-Cows frightens them on purpose and says it was me. It was not me.
I am Little-Minnow, sir. I am a hatchling of the Docks. I will not be small for ever. I am going to be a boat captain like Seeks-The-Channel. Are you smiling, sir? I am only looking.
Seeks-The-Channel, the boat captain, stands about ten paces east of here, sir. Please go and look at the boats with the captain. It is the best thing in the whole Docks.
Feldril Nethri, the Dunmer, works about fifteen paces north-east of here, miss. I am fond of Feldril. Feldril makes things from wood, and never says I am in the way.
Mind yourself, child. A vale deer lies dead about fifty paces south-east of here. Something killed it. I would not go and look at it with my hands empty.
If you want to gather, child, go far south, under the trees. Glowing mushrooms and creep cluster grow there, a hundred paces and a little more from where I sit.

About ten miles from Lilmoth there is a wall of mangroves, so thick that hardly anyone gets through. The old story says the roots were giant spiders once, child. I have always liked that one, because a root holds on the way a knot does.

Our Hist here is tended in the open, behind a wall. The tree-minder's post moves from one person to the next, so that a single person never listens to it alone. It is a kind way to do it, child. A person should not have to sit with something so large alone.

I am Plaits-The-Reed, child. I weave mats and baskets for the families of the Docks, and for the boats. I sit here on the south-west side, near the houses, out of the wind. My husband is out fishing. He will want his supper when he is back.
Wades-Late works about a dozen paces east-south-east of here, child. He works steadily.
Hey, warrior! Gourds grow about twenty paces north-west of here, so go and take them. Ushaa-Mei sells food as well, but she chased me off her stall, so I say the gourds are better.
Warrior, this is the Docks, and the north side by the spits is mine! A boar roots about a hundred paces north-east of here. Do you have a sword? Go and fight it, and let me watch!
I am Chases-Cows. The cows run because of me! I will be a warrior one day, a great one. Warrior, show me your sword and your scars!
Have you got scars? Tell me how you got every one of them. I will listen to all of it, I promise!

Little-Minnow sits about thirteen paces west-south-west of here, but Little-Minnow is a baby, so do not waste your time. Wades-Late works about twenty paces south of here. Wades-Late is the strongest person alive! Ask anyone!
Hereguard Plantation. West, ojel. A long way. About six hundred and forty paces. I would not walk it with a heavy pack.
There is a chest by the big ship. Seventy paces west-south-west of here. I do not go near it. Look if you want to, ojel.

I know the Docks, ojel, not all of Black Marsh. On the bigger docks a ship's crew is bought with somebody's months of owing. The harbourmaster calls it hiring. It takes paid work from free hands. I do not like it.
Wades-Late. I haul and I tie up boats. Half the Docks owe me coin, ojel. I wait for it. I am slow, but I am not forgetting.
I am Wades-Late, kin or ojel, it does not matter. I carry the loads here and tie the boats. I talk little.
I carry cargo and tie up boats, here on the south-east side, by the benches where loads are set down. Mind your feet, ojel.
The large ship is about seventy-five paces west. Its door leads aboard. Its crew left their cargo. I am still waiting to be paid for it.

You ask what this place is. It is a dock. I would say so more gently, outlander, if I were paid to. The north door stands about a dozen paces west of me, and another lies some six paces east-south-east, so you will not want for ways out.
The cooking pot hangs about a dozen paces south-east of where I stand. I know its place exactly, having been put where I may smell it and not sit by it.

Allow me to explain the law of this marsh as it was explained to me, with a great deal of patience and very little choice. When you lose what is not yours to lose, an arbitrator weighs the loss and turns it into months of labour, which they count in nushmeekos, and when those months are worked the matter is over. I have asked, more than once, who is doing the counting.

There was a time, outlander, when a foreigner without a licence was kept to the docks of Lilmoth and barred from the city itself. I mention it only because I, a guest of this marsh, find the arrangement so familiar that I could almost call it hospitality.

I am Feldril Nethri of the Dunmer. I came to this marsh to trade, which in my case now means carrying what other people unload. A cargo was lost, a loss was assessed. I work off the months it was turned into, though I have not yet been shown the sum of them. I ask for no pity, outlander. I would only like the number.

If it is kindness you are looking for, outlander, there is a child called Little-Minnow who sits about twenty paces south-west of me. She has been kind to me. I do not say that lightly of anyone in this place, nor do I forget it.
